subject: general
question: Who was the last Mughal emperor of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the last Mughal Emperor.

 
 
• He was deposed by the British and exiled to Burma (Rangoon) following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
 
 
• The Revolt of 1857 had made a futile attempt to declare him the Emperor of India.
 
• He was captured by the English and sent to Rangoon where he died in 1862.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Alamgir II**

 
 
• During the reign of Alamgir II, Delhi was occupied by Ahmed Shah Abdali.
 
• Ahmed Shah Abdali defeated Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**
 
• The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb was known as Abul Muzaffar Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb, commonly known as Aurangzeb or by his regional title Alamgir__.
 
 
• Mohi-ud-din Mohammed Aurangzeb was born on Oct. 24, 1618, at Dohad and was the third son of Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• Aurangzeb (1618-1707) was the sixth Mogul emperor of India and the last of the "Great Moguls."
 
• He extended the Mogul Empire to its farthest boundaries, but his reign was harsh and marked by revolts.
 
• He ruled over most of the Indian subcontinent during some parts of his reign, which lasted for 49 years from 1658 until he died in 1707.
 
• Mughal emperor Aurangzeb died in 1707 after a 49-year reign without officially declaring a crown prince.
 
 
 
• **Ahmad Shah Bahadur**
 
 
• During his reign, Ahmed Shah Abdali invaded India many times and Multan and Punjab were ceded to him.
